product.description: luminous ceiling panel: LED modules of 600 x 600 and 300 x 300 mm on an aluminium frame behind a light-diffusing white fabric, a seamless plane of light; tunable 2700 to 6500 K, set here to 3000 K; laid in the plenum over a laylight's etched glass, which the room draws
product.codeBasis: the maker's product name; a panel is built to size from its modules, frames and fabric (the specification sheet's bill of material), in over 170 sizes

light.fluxBasis: luminaire: 2574 lm/m2 (239 lm/ft2) at 3000 K, measured to IES LM-79-08 on the 900 x 900 mm panel and taken per square metre for the other sizes (the maker's note)
light.beamName: a Lambertian plane behind its diffusing fabric, 162 degree viewing angle

electrical.supply: 100 to 277 V AC to the maker's 100 W, 24 V DC power supplies
electrical.control: colour tuning and intensity by the LED module controller on PWM, 0-10 V or TouchDim; DALI through a DALI-to-PWM converter

housing.dimensionBasis: the room gives the extent of the laylight; the panel is 113 mm deep (the 900 x 3600 mm panel's height x width x depth, 929 x 3630 x 113 mm), so it fits a laylight's 0.20 plenum
housing.materials: extruded aluminium frame and crossbars, aluminium reflective inserts, light-diffusing white polyester fabric
housing.mounting: laid in the plenum over the laylight's glass, on brackets or cables

photometricFile.note: The maker publishes IES data by size; a luminous plane behind diffusing fabric is near Lambertian, as the record takes it.

sources.title: Color Kinetics, OneSpace gen2 Tunable White 900 x 3600 mm specification sheet (3/20/2026): 3000 K 2574 lm/m2, CRI 95, 39.5 to 41.1 W/m2, 162 degree viewing angle, 929 x 3630 x 113 mm; PWM, 0-10 V, TouchDim, DALI through a converter
Color Kinetics, OneSpace gen2 (product page): up to 2964 lm/m2, 90+ CRI, 2 step MacAdam, sizes 924 x 924 to 2424 x 9924 mm

unverified: The flux per square metre of sizes other than 900 x 900 mm is the maker's estimate from that panel, as its sheet says.
The etched laylight glass under the panel is the room's piece in Matter's glass; Light counts the panel's own output.
